issues.legal_issue: A group of trees qualifies as a grove for purposes of statutory retention when it forms a sufficiently compact and substantial unit that prevents the land from being primarily used for another purpose.
material_facts: The claimant sought to retain mango trees planted along both sides of a road, arguing that they constituted a grove.
The governing provision protected groves belonging to or held by a jagirdar, but did not define the term.
The trees were arranged along the road, and the record did not establish whether there were separate, sufficiently dense groups at particular locations.
issues.conclusion: A grove must consist of a sufficiently numerous and compact group of trees that gives the land the character of a grove and prevents it from being primarily used for another purpose. The trees need not bear fruit or have been planted by human agency. A line of roadside trees intended to shade the road is not, by itself, a grove, though a sufficiently dense cluster along the road may qualify.
issues.legal_principle: Under s. 5(b)(iv) of the Madhya Bharat Abolition of Jagirs Act, 1951, a grove belonging to or held by the jagirdar continues to belong to or be held by that person, and the land and appurtenant areas may be settled accordingly. The Court construed “grove” in its ordinary sense, drawing on dictionary meanings and on Daropadi v. Mannu Lal, A.I.R. 1929 All. 557; Kashi v. Jagoo Bai, A.I.R. 1934 All. 290; Shiv Sahai v. Hari Nandan, A.I.R. 1963 All. 413; and Hasan v. State of Bombay, 62 Bom. L.R. 617. The trees need not be fruit-bearing or planted by human agency, but must be sufficiently numerous and grouped so that the land is not primarily suited to another use.

rule.if: statutory_retention_claim and trees_belong_to_or_are_held_by_claimant and trees_form_compact_group and group_precludes_primary_non_grove_use

predicates.statutory_retention_claim: A person claims that a group of trees is protected from resumption under a land-resumption scheme.
predicates.trees_belong_to_or_are_held_by_claimant: The group of trees belongs to or is held by the person claiming retention.
predicates.trees_form_compact_group: The trees stand sufficiently close together to form a recognizable group.
predicates.group_precludes_primary_non_grove_use: The number and arrangement of the trees prevent the land they occupy from being primarily used for a purpose other than as grove land.

issues.definition: When a retention claim concerns trees belonging to or held by the claimant, the group qualifies as a grove if it is compact and prevents the land from being primarily used for another purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A claim that roadside trees form a grove cannot be rejected solely because the trees line a road without determining whether sufficiently dense clusters occur at particular locations.
material_facts: The revenue authorities and the High Court rejected the claim because the trees stood along both sides of a road.
The authorities did not determine whether there were groups of trees at particular locations along the road that were sufficiently numerous and close together to constitute groves.
The claimant contended that such groups might exist, and the Court considered that contention worthy of examination.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the High Court judgment and order were set aside, and the matter was remanded for a finding on whether groups of trees at any locations along the road were sufficient in number and proximity to constitute a grove or groves, with the parties given an opportunity to present further evidence.
issues.legal_principle: In applying s. 5(b)(iv) of the Madhya Bharat Abolition of Jagirs Act, 1951, roadside placement does not by itself resolve whether trees form a grove. Where the claim may depend on distinct clusters and no inquiry has been made into those clusters, the factual question must be examined before the claim is rejected.

predicates.appeal_from_rejection_of_grove_claim: A person appeals after a claim that trees constitute a grove has been rejected.
predicates.rejection_based_only_on_roadside_alignme: The claim was rejected on the basis that the trees stood along a road.
predicates.possible_tree_clusters_not_examined: The decision-makers did not determine whether sufficiently numerous and close groups of trees existed at particular locations, although the claim could depend on that question.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a rejection based only on roadside alignment and possible tree clusters were not examined, the appeal is allowed and the case is remanded for factual inquiry.
